editorial.headline: Building the Framework of Indonesia’s Non-Fishing Ports
editorial.standfirst: This is the construction category for the hard infrastructure of non-fishing ports—open nationally to foreign investment, while Bali’s risk treatment keeps it outside the island-wide PMA bar.
editorial.body:
At its core, this is the construction activity for the built fabric of a non-fishing port. It covers new construction, maintenance and reconstruction of jetty and trestle structures, as well as port infrastructure at sea, river and lake locations. The boundary also reaches into the water: coastal or in-water fill undertaken for port-building construction is expressly included. In plain terms, it covers the works that create, restore and maintain the physical framework of a port.

The recorded scope is deliberately wide within that framework. It includes waterways and canals, ports and river-route facilities, marinas, docks and locks; it embraces dredging, normalisation and maintenance of rivers, ports, swamps, lakes, shipping lanes, basins and canals. Such work may be light, medium or heavy. Supporting port buildings, including dedicated terminals, sit within the same activity. The connecting idea is infrastructure linked to a non-fishing port and its waterborne setting.

Registration access is listed for Large, Micro, Small and Medium scales. The activity is not reserved for one business scale, even though its scope reaches from maintenance work to substantial port infrastructure. Nationally, it is marked open to PMA, with a foreign ownership ceiling of 100%. The national PMA source recorded is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021: the activity is open at the national level without a foreign-equity cap below full ownership.

Bali requires a closer reading rather than a blanket conclusion drawn from national openness. The province’s permanent, island-wide rule blocks PMA registration for all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities. This activity is not blocked under that moratorium. The Bali record says that at the Large scale its OSS risk is Medium-High/High, placing it outside the moratorium’s stated Low and Medium-Low reach. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The practical position is plain: a foreign investor can register this activity in Bali today; the local record treats it as available while identifying its higher-risk position at the Large scale.
editorial.pullQuote: A foreign investor can register this activity in Bali today, because its stated risk position keeps it outside the island-wide PMA moratorium.
